newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy unions meet govt on metalworkers dispute.
newsitem.headline: Italy unions meet govt on metalworkers dispute.

text.p: Leaders of Italy's three big trades union federations began a meeting with Prime Minister Romano Prodi and cabinet officials on Friday to discuss a long-standing metal and engineering workers dispute.
The meeting was requested by the CGIL-CISL-UIL confederation earlier this week.

It was not clear if the employers federation Confindustria or the metal and engineering sector's management group, Federmeccanica, would join the talks later in the day or have separate talks with the government.
Prodi was joined at the meeting by Labour Minister Tiziano Treu, Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni, and Industry Minister Pierluigi Bersani.
The pay dispute has been dragging on since June.
In December the government suggested that management give workers an average 200,000 lire per month pay increase.
Unions, which had been seeking a 230,000 lire increase, accepted the proposals but management refused it as inflationary.
The dispute, which involves some 1.7 million workers, is expected to set the tone for pay deals in a number of other Italian industrial sectors.
Metalworkers unions have already staged several stoppages to press their claims and the main union federations have threatened to call a general strike. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
